title: Sabrina Carpenter Says Goodbye to Her Hero Dolly Parton
summary:
Have you ever had a hero — someone you look up to so much that meeting them feels like a dream? That's how Sabrina Carpenter felt about Dolly Parton, the country music legend who died at age 80.

Sabrina and Dolly worked together on a song called "Please Please Please." They even shot a music video together, dressed like the characters from the movie Thelma & Louise. Sabrina shared pictures from that day and wrote a sad, sweet message: "oh dolly 💔 the only thing i could say after we first met was 'she really is an angel walking the earth' and 'we look like we could be sisters!'"

Dolly felt the same way! She told Rolling Stone magazine that their voices sounded so similar, she couldn't tell which part was hers and which was Sabrina's. She also said they looked like relatives. "She looks like she could be my little sister," Dolly said. "We're little women, doing big things."

During the video shoot, they spent hours talking in a pickup truck. Their mics had to be turned off because they were chatting so much! Dolly gave Sabrina advice: "Don't ever sacrifice your morals and your soul and your principles and your own values."

Sabrina says she'll keep Dolly's wisdom and humor "in my pocket for the rainy days." She ended her message with "i will always love you" — a nod to Dolly's most famous song. It's a sad time, but also a celebration of a wonderful friendship.
why_it_matters: It shows that even famous people can look up to heroes, and that kind advice from someone we admire can stay with us for a long time.
